LESSON: SKIPPING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.4: Skipping
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Skipping, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can apparatus used in skipping be made more interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify different ways of skipping in different directions

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Skipping in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. skip in different directions for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Skipping in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make patterns while skipping in different ways,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Skipping in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate skipping in different directions for balance and strength.  Learners to talk about skipping in different directions. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.  Learners to skip in different ways. Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability.  Learners to play games involving skipping skills. Leaners with mobility difficulties and those on mobility devices could perform an alternative corresponding activity while singing.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Skipping together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
 Unity: The learner cooperates with peers while skipping.

 Peace: The learner avoids hurting others by observing safety while playing games involving skipping.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Gender issues in education: The learner shows respect for gender equality while playing games in skipping with peers.

Link to other subjects:

Mathematics activities: The learner learns concepts of shapes and patterns.
